rfi.title: Nepal glacier disaster toll passes 1,000 as calls for climate justice grow
rfi.description: The death toll from last week's devastating Himalayan glacial floods passed 1,000 on Tuesday, as Chinese and Nepali teams searched for survivors. Nepal's foreign minister said the disaster was "a warning signal" of the growing risks posed by climate change.

rfi.title: DRC school year begins amid Ebola, strikes and conflict
rfi.description: Millions of students returned to school across the Democratic Republic of Congo on Tuesday, but the new term began amid an Ebola outbreak affecting six provinces, a teachers’ strike call and continuing conflict in the east. In AFC/M23-controlled territories, the movement organised the return to classrooms even as Kinshasa continued to pay primary and secondary school teachers.

rfi.title: French clubs cash in as Ligue 1 transfer window comes to a close
rfi.description: The transfer window for French football clubs closed on Tuesday evening after three months of trading that saw the 18 Ligue 1 sides splash out €522 million and reap €894 million in player sales.

rfi.title: French schools start new year in shadow of summer cyberattack
rfi.description: Millions of pupils are returning to classrooms across France on Tuesday for the start of the new school year, with some schools forced to fall back on paper timetables and registers after a major cyberattack disrupted education systems over the summer.

rfi.title: Russia’s return to G20 talks unsettles Europe as Iran and trade tensions loom
rfi.description: Russia's presence at the opening of G20 meetings in North Carolina sparked pushback from Europe on Monday, adding fresh tension to talks already clouded by the Iran war and US President Donald Trump's trade policies.

rfi.title: Ukraine air defences top agenda as EU ministers meet in Ireland
rfi.description: European Union defence and foreign ministers gathering in Ireland this week are set to focus on strengthening Ukraine’s air defences, as concern grows over both Russia’s intensifying bombardment and what European officials see as a widening campaign of destabilisation across the continent.

rfi.title: France takes aim at fast-fashion giants with new pricing penalties
rfi.description: France will start imposing fees on ultra-fast fashion from Tuesday, with charges set to rise to almost €20 per garment as the government steps up pressure on major Asian e-commerce platforms including Shein.

rfi.title: From labels to Netflix, how Quebec's fight to protect French collides with US trade
rfi.description: French-language protections in Quebec have emerged as an unlikely source of friction between Canada and the United States, bringing rules designed to protect French in overwhelmingly English-speaking North America into a much bigger fight over trade.

rfi.title: No more Messi nights for Argentina as skipper says adios to national squad
rfi.description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino led the tributes to Argentina skipper Lionel Messi, who announced his retirement from international football just over a month after playing in the 2026 World Cup final.

rfi.title: 'Devoted servant of the nation': Former French PM Édouard Balladur dies aged 97
rfi.description: Former French prime minister Édouard Balladur died in Paris late Monday at the age of 97, his family said. Born in Turkey, he served as former president Francois Mitterrand's last prime minister from March 1993 to May 1995, carrying out several major privatisations of state companies, and unsuccessfully ran for the top job in 1995.

rfi.title: Ten years after Gabon’s post-election violence, painful questions remain
rfi.description: Ten years on, victims of violence that followed president Ali Bongo’s disputed re-election in Gabon are still demanding truth and justice. Questions also remain over the possible involvement of French nationals and the response of the French authorities.

rfi.title: Niger coup attempt: 'Russians saved the day' analyst tells RFI
rfi.description: Niger’s military government has survived its most serious internal challenge since seizing power in 2023, after Russian paramilitaries helped loyalist forces crush last Saturday's attempted coup in the capital, Niamey. RFI spoke to an expert who explains how this episode has left General Abdourahamane Tiani’s junta weakened and more dependent on Russia.

rfi.title: French high schools scramble to work out rules as phone ban takes effect
rfi.description: The new school year starts on Tuesday in France, and with it comes a new rule: mobile phones will no longer be allowed in high schools. The ban came into force a week before the first day of term, leaving schools with little time to work out how to put it into practice.

rfi.title: France's international photojournalism festival founder Leroy dies aged 69
rfi.description: Tributes have been pouring in for Jean-François Leroy, the founder of the Visa pour l'image photojournalism festival, who died on Monday at the age of 69.

rfi.title: UN committee presents legal case for broad slavery reparations
rfi.description: Countries are "legally obliged" to provide broad reparations for harms resulting from both direct and indirect involvement in the transatlantic African slave trade, a United Nations committee has said. This comes amid a fresh interpretation of a global accord, published on Monday.

rfi.title: What the SDF’s dissolution means for Syria’s Kurds and neighbouring Turkey
rfi.description: Nearly a week after the Syrian Democratic Forces agreed to dissolve, the consequences are beginning to take shape for Syria's Kurds and neighbouring Turkey. As the former US-backed force is absorbed into the Syrian state, questions remain over what the country's Kurds have secured in return – from language and political rights to protections for women – and what the end of more than a decade of Kurdish-led autonomy means for Turkey's own conflict with Kurdish militants.

rfi.title: Dissident militia in Colombia says kidnapped French Foreign Legion soldier alive
rfi.description: Colombian rebels have claimed responsibility for kidnapping a Colombian soldier serving in the French Foreign Legion, saying he is alive and in good health nearly a month after he was seized in the south-west of the country. However they warned the government against any military intervention.

rfi.title: EU hides disappointment after Iceland's 'No' vote
rfi.description: The EU put a brave face Sunday on Iceland's vote against restarting membership talks, but the outcome was a bitter pill to swallow – robbing Brussels of a hoped-for success story while delighting its eurosceptic critics.

euronews.title: End of the Cook era: Apple has a new CEO for the first time in 15 years
euronews.description: Apple's top job has changed hands for the first time in 15 years, with John Ternus succeeding Tim Cook, the man who built the iPhone maker into a wildly successful tech giant.

euronews.title: Mass burials of unidentified victims continue in Nepal as death toll exceeds 1,000 one week after flash floods
euronews.description: Many were outraged and expressed their disapproval after the government revealed it intended to carry out mass “temporary” burials of the deceased. Nepal’s largely Hindu community objected to the measure which they say goes against religious traditions.

euronews.title: Tyler Robinson pleads not guilty as judge clears path for death penalty in Charlie Kirk assassination case
euronews.description: Robinson, seen as the sole suspect in the 2025 assassination of right-wing activist Charlie Kirk, entered a not guilty plea after a judge gave the green light for prosecutors to advance towards the death penalty as the case goes to trial.

euronews.title: How Taiwan's AI stock boom has ordinary people borrowing to invest
euronews.description: People across Taiwan are taking out loans and even remortgaging their homes to chase gains in an AI-fuelled stock boom — and not everyone is coming out ahead.

euronews.title: ‘Paradox of progress’: What it will take to turn renewables boom into a real drop in emissions
euronews.description: A major new UN report details the risks of overshooting 1.5°C of warming – and how we can limit them.

euronews.title: Mediterranean in flux: four decades of data reveal climate change impact
euronews.description: Spanish scientists, working with colleagues in Europe and the US, have compiled data from 46 oceanographic missions (1976–2018) to track how the Mediterranean is changing under climate change.

euronews.title: Prominent pro-democracy Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong pleads guilty in second national security law case
euronews.description: Wong, already serving prison time for a separate case, pleaded guilty to a second offence under Beijing’s 2020 National Security law, which could see his sentence extended by a minimum of three years and up to life imprisonment.

euronews.title: What's behind France's plan to survey school children on sexual violence?
euronews.description: For the first time, France's annual school questionnaire on bullying — which has been handed out to pupils since 2023 — will include questions on sexual violence. Pupils will be able to choose whether or not to they wish to remain anonymous in this questionnaire, to be distributed in November

euronews.title: Zelenskyy warns ‘Russian airspace will effectively be closing’
euronews.description: The Ukrainian president warned airlines, insurers and foreign governments that the growing scale of Kyiv’s drone operations would make Russian airspace increasingly unsafe for aircraft.

euronews.title: Spanish government approves €309 million aid package for Ceuta amid migrant crisis
euronews.description: Spain's Economy Minister said the aid package represents a 'shock response' designed to meet the demands of social organisations and the city government.

euronews.title: US launches new strikes in southern Iran, Tehran responds with attacks across region
euronews.description: The US military launched new waves of strikes on military installations along Iran's southern coast. Tehran responded immediately with missile and drone attacks in Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait, sparking a new flare-up of hostilities and threats from both sides.

euronews.title: Ryanair's Boeing 737 stairs tied to hundreds of passenger falls, study says
euronews.description: Ryanair's Boeing 737 comes with retractable onboard stairs that cut costs and turnaround times, but an Italian safety study has linked them to hundreds of passenger falls since 2021.

euronews.title: SCO challenges West as diverse group of nations pursues multipolar future
euronews.description: The summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, which represents almost half of the world’s population, ended with an aim to signal the rise of a global powerhouse challenging the West. Yet the SCO's diversity also revealed significant disagreements and divergent interests.

euronews.title: Von der Leyen pledges response to Russian hybrid attacks ahead of Rutte meeting
euronews.description: As Germany formally blames Russia for a hybrid warfare incident involving an explosive-laden drone at one of its airports, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will meet NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte to discuss a coordinated response.

euronews.title: Russia's Starlink copycat has failed so far but still threatens Ukraine
euronews.description: Russia's homegrown Starlink rival has suffered a fresh setback, with an entire batch of satellites failing to reach orbit — but even a partially working system could still sharpen Russian strikes on Ukraine.

euronews.title: Brussels says €90 billion loan for Ukraine is enough for now amid growing doubts
euronews.description: The longevity of the EU's €90 billion support loan for Ukraine is in serious doubt as Russia escalates the war and drives up material costs. Brussels says the financial plan remains sufficient "for the moment".

euronews.title: Russia behind attempted drone 'attack' at Leipzig airport, Berlin says
euronews.description: Germany has for months reported suspicious drone sightings over military and industrial sites, but an incident at Leipzig/Halle Airport on the night of 4-5 August raised the alarm as a drone found there carried explosives.

euronews.title: EU’s green fashion rules face test as global emissions rise 6.3%
euronews.description: The findings of a report on fashion data pose a political challenge for the EU, which has made textiles one of the testing grounds for its broader push to move from a linear economy – make, sell and throw away – towards a circular one.

lemonde.title: Le monde devra tout faire pour revenir sous le seuil de 1,5 °C de réchauffement après l’avoir dépassé, avertit l’ONU
lemonde.description: Le Programme des Nations unies pour l’environnement prend acte du dépassement prochain de l’objectif le plus ambitieux de l’accord de Paris, et dessine une nouvelle trajectoire afin de repasser dessous avant la fin du siècle. Elle implique des efforts gigantesques et des transformations radicales.

lemonde.title: Les gardiens de la révolution répliquent à des bombardements américains sur des positions iraniennes
lemonde.description: L’Iran a attaqué des bases militaires des Etats-Unis dans le Golfe après la conclusion d’une salve de frappes américaines contre lui, la deuxième en quelques jours. Quelques heures auparavant, le président iranien, Massoud Pezeshkian, avait plaidé pour une reprise des négociations.

lemonde.title: En Israël, la droite, menacée de défaite aux législatives, se déchire et se radicalise
lemonde.description: En amont des élections législatives du 27 octobre, des tensions apparaissent au sein de la coalition gouvernementale, notamment entre le premier ministre, Benyamin Nétanyahou, et son ministre de la sécurité nationale, Itamar Ben Gvir. De la droite à l’extrême droite, chacun durcit son discours pour remobiliser ses sympathisants.

lemonde.title: Au Royaume-Uni, Andy Burnham fustige des décennies de « privatisations » et promet de mettre fin au « déclin » du pays
lemonde.description: Lors de son premier discours devant le Parlement, mardi 1er septembre, le nouveau premier ministre britannique s’est engagé à redonner de « l’espoir » à ses concitoyens, sans annoncer de mesures précises. Le budget qui déterminera la politique du gouvernement sera connu fin octobre.

lemonde.title: Aux Etats-Unis, J. D. Vance livre une plaidoirie sinueuse devant une organisation de juifs républicains
lemonde.description: Invité par la Republican Jewish Coalition à Las Vegas, lundi 31 août, le vice-président américain a tenté d’expliquer sa ligne sur la relation avec Israël et la montée de l’antisémitisme, tout en préservant ses intérêts de favori de la future primaire de son parti.

lemonde.title: Les films à l’affiche : « Retour avant 15 heures », « Trois adieux », « Lettres d’amour de ma grand-mère »…
lemonde.description: Chaque mercredi dans La Matinale, les journalistes cinéma du « Monde » livrent leurs critiques des œuvres à découvrir en salle. Aujourd’hui, la réalisatrice espagnole Isabel Coixet livre une méditation intimiste et sensible sur la condition humaine.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : les sanctions allemandes envers la Russie sont « une nouvelle erreur grossière », dit Vladimir Poutine
lemonde.description: Berlin, qui a formellement accusé Moscou d’avoir envoyé un drone chargé d’explosifs début août à l’aéroport de Leipzig, a annoncé des mesures de rétorsion contre la Russie.

lemonde.title: Gaël Monfils passe le premier tour de l’US Open et fête ses 40 ans avec le public new-yorkais
lemonde.description: Le vétéran français, 311ᵉ mondial, a dignement célébré son anniversaire en éliminant le Paraguayen Adolfo Daniel Vallejo (60ᵉ) en quatre sets, dont un 6-0 pour finir la rencontre. Ses adieux en Grand Chelem attendront donc encore au moins un match de plus.

lemonde.title: Le président chinois Xi Jinping commence un marathon diplomatique, des régimes hostiles à l’Occident jusqu’à la Maison Blanche
lemonde.description: Au sommet de l’Organisation de coopération de Shanghaï, qui s’est tenu lundi et mardi au Kirghizistan, Xi Jinping a réaffirmé son opposition à l’impérialisme américain quelques semaines avant sa rencontre avec Donald Trump, à Washington.

lemonde.description: En août, plusieurs maires, dont ceux de Chartres, Dijon, Strasbourg ou encore Amiens, ont exprimé leur opposition à la venue du chanteur de 67 ans dans leurs villes respectives.

lemonde.title: Assassinat de Charlie Kirk : un juge américain statue que le suspect, Tyler Robinson, sera jugé
lemonde.description: L’homme de 23 ans, qui risque la peine de mort, a plaidé non coupable des charges qui pèsent contre lui.

lemonde.title: Après la séquence de cyberattaques par des IA en test, OpenAI va « bientôt » lancer son modèle de pointe, Astra, mais corseté
lemonde.description: Le créateur de ChatGPT n’a pas dévoilé de date de lancement pour ce un modèle encore plus puissant. La société, qui souligne qu’Astra « n’était pas impliqué » dans l’attaque contre Hugging Face, promet un contrôle renforcé.

lemonde.title: Hongkong : Joshua Wong, figure du mouvement prodémocratie, plaide coupable de collusion avec l’étranger
lemonde.description: L’ancien leader étudiant de 29 ans, qui purge déjà une peine de près de cinq ans de prison pour subversion, risque désormais la prison à perpétuité.

lemonde.title: Plongée dans les élevages industriels de mouches et de ténébrions : « Elever des insectes, ce n’est pas une lubie »
lemonde.description: « La planète des insectes » (3/6). Le plus gros élevage d’insectes au monde se trouve en France. Dans cette filière en pleine restructuration, des entreprises veulent convaincre des atouts des arthropodes pour l’alimentation animale.

lemonde.title: Au Nicaragua, une réforme du président Ortega exclut les opposants des élections et porte le mandat présidentiel de six à sept ans
lemonde.description: Le texte voté à l’unanimité par l’Assemblée nationale exclut des élections ceux qui participent à des « actes putschistes » ou de « trahison de la patrie » ou qui sollicitent une « intervention militaire » étrangère.

lemonde.title: Bosnie : plusieurs milliers de personnes rendent hommage à l’ex-chef militaire serbe bosnien Ratko Mladic, condamné pour génocide
lemonde.description: Un défilé a eu lieu, mardi, à Banja Luka. L’ex-général, condamné pour génocide par le Tribunal pénal international pour l’ex-Yougoslavie, est mort le 27 août à 84 ans.

france24fr.title: Aux États-Unis, Tyler Robinson, l'assassin présumé de Charlie Kirk, sera bien jugé
france24fr.description: Un juge de l'Utah a ordonné mardi le renvoi en procès de Tyler Robinson, 23 ans, accusé du meurtre du militant ultra conservateur Charlie Kirk en septembre 2025. Le suspect, qui risque la peine de mort, a plaidé non coupable.

france24fr.title: Midterms 2026 : le vote par correspondance est en danger, avertit un lanceur d'alerte
france24fr.description: À deux mois des élections de mi-mandat aux États-Unis, un lanceur d'alerte affirme mardi que la Poste américaine a développé "en secret" des systèmes informatiques de manière "bâclée et précipitée" pour se conformer à un décret de Donald Trump visant à encadrer plus sévèrement le vote par correspondance. Des millions d'Américains pourraient ainsi être privés de bulletin de vote à distance.

france24fr.title: Au terme du G20 Finance, les ministres plaident pour la liberté de navigation dans le détroit d'Ormuz
france24fr.description: À l'issue de deux jours de réunions au G20 à Asheville, les ministres des Finances ont défendu mardi une navigation sûre et sans coût dans le détroit d'Ormuz. La présence du ministre russe des Finances lors du sommet n'a "pas eu d'impact" sur l'issue des discussions, a affirmé le secrétaire américain au Trésor, Scott Bessent.

france24fr.title: Drones ukrainiens : Zelensky met en garde l'aviation civile, Poutine évoque une menace "terroriste"
france24fr.description: Le président ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky a prévenu mardi l'aviation civile que "les jours sûrs dans le ciel russe sont révolus" en raison de l'intensification des frappes de drones ukrainiens sur la Russie. Son homologue russe Vladimir Poutine a qualifié cet avertissement de "déclaration de terrorisme d'État".

france24fr.title: Israël affirme avoir arrêté le chef de la sécurité intérieure du Hamas à Gaza
france24fr.description: L'armée israélienne a mené des frappes aériennes qui ont fait au moins quatre morts mardi dans la ville de Gaza. Lors de cette opération, Moueïn al-Arabid, le chef du service de sécurité intérieure du Hamas, a été interpellé à son domicile, a annoncé le Premier ministre israélien, Benjamin Netanyahu. Le mouvement a dénoncé une "opération criminelle".

france24fr.title: Tapisserie de Bayeux : les dessous d'une œuvre unique
france24fr.description: Emmanuel Macron est attendu ce mercredi à Londres pour l'inauguration de l'exposition consacrée à la Tapisserie de Bayeux. Une œuvre monumentale vieille de presque 1000 ans qui raconte la conquête de l'Angleterre par Guillaume le Conquérant.

france24fr.title: En direct : l'Iran attaque des bases des États-Unis après de nouvelles frappes américaines
france24fr.description: Jordanie, Irak, Bahreïn... L'Iran a attaqué mercredi des bases militaires des États-Unis dans le Golfe après la conclusion d'une salve de frappes américaines contre lui, la deuxième en quelques jours. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Lac Ontario ou Lac Amérique : Google a-t-il adopté la dénomination voulue par Trump ?
france24fr.description: Après avoir unilatéralement rebaptisé le golfe du Mexique en "golfe d’Amérique", Donald Trump s'attaque au Canada. Son récent décret visant à renommer le célèbre "lac Ontario" en "lac Amérique" a provoqué un véritable casse-tête pour les applications de cartographie comme Google et Apple Maps ... et donné naissance à de folles rumeurs de représailles maritimes.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : accord avec le FMI en vue d'un programme d'aide de plus de 2 milliards de dollars
france24fr.description: Le FMI est parvenu à un accord avec le gouvernement du Sénégal en vue de la mise en place d'un programme d'aide "d'environ 2,2 milliards de dollars" pour la période 2026-2029, a annoncé le Fonds monétaire international.  Cette annonce intervient près de trois ans après la suspension par l’institution de son dernier prêt, suite à la révélation par Dakar d’une dette cachée contractée par l’administration précédente. A Dakar, les précisions de Sarah Sakho.

france24fr.title: Basket : le champion de France Monaco exclu du monde professionnel
france24fr.description: Le champion de France en titre de basket, l'AS Monaco, exclu de la Ligue nationale de basket pour raisons financières, a annoncé mardi se porter candidat à une place dans le championnat de Nationale 1, le troisième niveau du basket français. La "Roca Team" espère rebondir et "retrouver sa place au sommet".

france24fr.title: Exclusif : au Népal, des cimetières temporaires pour les corps sans nom
france24fr.description: À Bharatpur, la forêt s’est transformée en cimetière improvisé. Après la crue dévastatrice du 26 août, les morgues débordent et les corps, parfois emportés sur des centaines de kilomètres, arrivent par dizaines. Les autorités n’ont d’autre choix que d’inhumer provisoirement ces victimes sans nom. Avant chaque enterrement, l'ADN est prélevé, un numéro inscrit sur la tombe, ultime repère pour des familles qui espèrent encore. Près de 300 corps ont été retrouvés, mais seuls neuf ont, pour l’instant

france24fr.title: Incursions de drones, sabotages, cyberattaques, espionnages : Moscou pousse-t-il l'Europe à bout ?
france24fr.description: Au lendemain d’une nouvelle attaque massive sur Kiev et sa région qui a fait 12 morts, Volodymyr Zelensky a appellé ses partenaires à lui fournir davantage de capacités de défense balistiques. La tension est encore montée d’un cran entre les Européens et la Russie, alors que le gouvernement allemand a accusé les services secrets russes d'être responsables de la tentative d'attentat au drone explosif contre l'aéroport de Leipzig début août. Le Secrétaire général de l'OTAN Mark Rutte s'est égaleme

france24fr.title: L'Iran promet une riposte "décisive" après de nouvelles frappes américaines
france24fr.description: Les États-Unis ont lancé mardi une nouvelle salve ⁠de bombardements contre des ​cibles iraniennes autour du détroit d'Ormuz, alimentant le risque d'une escalade des hostilités après les échanges de tirs survenus au cours du week-end, alors que Téhéran a promis de répondre aux attaques de Washington.

france24fr.title: Berlin accuse Moscou d'être derrière l'attaque au drone explosif à Leipzig
france24fr.description: L'Allemagne a annoncé mardi des mesures de rétorsion contre la Russie, après l'avoir officiellement accusée d'avoir envoyé un drone chargé d'explosifs début août à l'aéroport de Leipzig, une plateforme militaire clé pour l'armée allemande et pour l'Otan.

france24fr.title: Sous la pression, Patrick Bruel renonce finalement à sa tournée
france24fr.description: Le ⁠chanteur Patrick Bruel, mis ​en examen en juin pour viol, tentative de ​viol, agression sexuelle et harcèlement sexuel, a annoncé mardi l'annulation de sa tournée de concerts en France qui devait commencer ​début ‌octobre.

france24fr.title: Reportage exclusif : au Népal, les corps non identifiés commencent à être enterrés à Bharatpur
france24fr.description: Au Népal, plusieurs jours après la catastrophe, certains corps retrouvés sont déjà dans un état avancé de décomposition. Les morgues des principales villes du pays arrivent à saturation. Face à l’afflux des dépouilles, les autorités ont donné l'autorisation de les enterrer sans identification formelle, notamment pour limiter les risques sanitaires et les fortes odeurs. Les envoyés spéciaux de France 24 se sont rendus sur l’un de ces sites d’inhumation à Bharatpur, dans le sud du Népal.

france24fr.title: L'Iran a-t-il adapté des lance-roquettes pour miner le détroit d'Ormuz ?
france24fr.description: Les bombardements américains menés dimanche sur l’île de Larak ont été justifiés par la nécessité de détruire de nouvelles capacités pour miner le détroit d’Ormuz. Le recours par l’Iran à des lance-roquettes pour déployer des mines marines dans ce passage stratégique serait inédit, mais pas impossible. Même si certains experts restent sceptiques.

france24fr.title: Kenya : l'aéroport de Nairobi paralysé par une grève des travailleurs
france24fr.description: 🇰🇪 Au Kenya, une grève des travailleurs du secteur aérien provoque depuis dimanche d’importants retards et annulations de vols. Cette mobilisation d’employés dénonçant leurs conditions de travail perturbe fortement les déplacements de passagers.

zeit.title: Kita-Bericht: Zwei Drittel aller Kitas haben nicht genug Personal
zeit.description: Einer Umfrage zufolge fehlen mehr als 100.000 pädagogische Fachkräfte in den Kitas. In mehr als der Hälfte mussten deshalb zuletzt Betreuungszeiten gekürzt werden.

zeit.title: Wettervorhersage: Wechselhaftes Wetter in Hessen – Süden wird sommerlich warm
Rhein-Erft-Kreis: Polizei ermittelt nach Störung an Umspannwerk in NRW
zeit.description: Nach einer Störung an einem Umspannwerk im Rhein-Erft-Kreis schließt die Polizei einen technischen Defekt aus. Es gebe Hinweise auf eine vorsätzliche Tat.

zeit.title: Polizeieinsatz in Augsburg: Explosion in Gebäudedurchgang: mehrere Menschen verletzt
Festival: Welche Literaturstars man jetzt in Berlin erleben kann
Zukunftsentscheid: Thering will Klimaziel 2040 wieder kippen
Wetter: Stürmische Tage im Norden – Gewitter und Regen im Anmarsch
Feuerwehr-Einsatz: Brand in Reinsdorfer Lagerhallen – Löscharbeiten dauern an
Kritik am FIFA-Präsidenten: Carro: «Wir führen jetzt einen Kampf gegen Infantino»
Schwerer Unfall: Motorradfahrer prallt gegen Baum – lebensgefährlich verletzt
Bundesregierung und Russland: Schrecken die deutschen Gegenmaßnahmen Russland ab?
zeit.description: Die Bundesregierung präsentiert ein neues Maßnahmenpaket, um gegen Russland vorzugehen.  Reicht das? Und: Welchen Einfluss hat KI auf Ihr Gehalt?

zeit.title: Elbvertiefung: Der tägliche Newsletter aus Hamburg: Warum jetzt U-Boote in Hamburg für Stau sorgen
zeit.description: Die Elbvertiefung am Mittwoch – mit einer Friedensforscherin zur Vorsorge im Kriegsfall und aufregenden Versuchen an einer Hamburger Grundschule.

zeit.title: Ikone der Pop-Art: Die Welt mit David Hockneys Augen sehen
zeit.description: Mit platinblonden Haaren und legendären Anzügen: Der Maler David Hockney zählt zu den wichtigsten Künstlern des 20. Jahrhunderts. Wie er zur Ikone der Pop-Art wurde.

zeit.title: Salbei-Parmesan-Gnocchi: Nie wieder Angst vor Gnocchi haben
zeit.description: Amateurköche haben häufig großen Respekt vor Gnocchi. Dieses Rezept beweist, wie einfach und günstig die selbst gemachten Kartoffelkissen sein können. Und diese Soße!

zeit.title: Studie: Psychische Belastung gefährdet Ausbildungserfolg
zeit.description: 90 Prozent der Auszubildenden sind mit ihrer Ausbildung zufrieden. Gleichzeitig fühlt sich ein Teil emotional davon belastet. Das kann auch Folgen für den Betrieb haben.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Dieser Hitzesommer zeigt: Weil die Gletscher verschwinden, müssen wir mehr Staudämme bauen
nzz.description: Die Alpen gelten als Refugium für Ausflügler und Touristen. Durch die Gletscherschmelze und den Wassermangel während Hitzewellen könnten sie aber eine viel wichtigere Bedeutung erlangen – vorausgesetzt, ihre Bewohner handeln.

nzz.title: PODCAST «NZZ GEOPOLITIK» - Chinas stiller Krieg um Taiwan hat längst begonnen
nzz.description: Peking versucht mit allen Mitteln, Taiwan zu destabilisieren, ohne dass auch nur ein Schuss fällt. Der Sinologe und Geheimdienstexperte Jürgen Kremb schildert im Podcast «NZZ Geopolitik», wie China die Insel mit Cyberangriffen, Desinformation und Spionage unterwandert.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Deutschland reagiert klug auf Russlands Aggression
nzz.description: Nach der Attacke in Leipzig schliesst die deutsche Regierung zwei russische Einrichtungen. Sie zeigt damit Entschlossenheit, ohne die Schraube zu überdrehen. Eine Äusserung von Kanzler Friedrich Merz hinterlässt aber einen Nachgeschmack.

nzz.title: Iranische Videos rufen zur Ermordung von Barron Trump auf – was steckt dahinter?
nzz.description: In iranischen Staatsmedien wird dem Sohn des amerikanischen Präsidenten mit dem Tod gedroht. Gegen den Sohn des israelischen Ministerpräsidenten Benjamin Netanyahu soll es gar ein Mordkomplott gegeben haben.

nzz.title: Wenn der Union Jack zum «Sicherheitsrisiko» wird – in Grossbritannien tobt ein Kulturkampf um Flaggen
nzz.description: Erst waren überall Gaza-Fahnen zu sehen, nun hissen nationalistische Gruppen massenweise britische Flaggen. Das sorgt für Skandale, Randale und Verbote.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - «Lex UBS»: Der Kommissionsentscheid ist ein Schritt in die richtige Richtung, aber noch kein Befreiungsschlag
nzz.description: Die Wirtschaftskommission des Ständerats erteilt dem Vorschlag des Bundesrates für die Kapitalausstattung der Grossbank eine Absage. Doch ihre eigene Antwort auf die Pläne des Bundesrats weist ebenfalls Mängel auf.

nzz.title: Alles dreht sich um Xi: SCO-Gipfel in Bischkek zeigt gewachsenen Einfluss von Chinas Präsidenten
nzz.description: Bei dem Regionalgipfel in Kirgistan präsentiert sich China als Quelle der Stabilität in einer unruhigen Welt. Von dem Druck der USA, seine Unterstützung für Iran und Russland zu reduzieren, lässt es sich nicht beeindrucken.

nzz.title: Gefangen in der Dystopie: Über einen Monat nach dem Ansturm auf Ceuta nimmt die Gewalt zu
nzz.description: In Spaniens nordafrikanischer Exklave leiden Flüchtlinge wie Bewohner. Den Stadtfeiertag Ceutas am Mittwoch will die Opposition zu landesweiten Protesten gegen die Regierung nutzen.

nzz.title: Das Römische Reich wird bedrängt, bei den Parthern herrscht eine Sklavin, und in Palästina predigt Jesus vom Ende der Zeit: Um das Jahr null kam die Welt ins Wanken
nzz.description: Geschichte aus Geschichten: In seinem neuen Buch skizziert Moritz Aisslinger das Panorama einer Zeit, in der Europas Fundamente gelegt wurden.

nzz.title: Die Schweiz ist ein Magnet für multinationale Konzerne. Doch deren Unzufriedenheit mit dem Standort wächst
nzz.description: Ein neuer Bericht von McKinsey benennt die grössten Gefahren für den Wirtschaftsstandort. Der neue Chefökonom des Bundes sagt, warum ihm besonders ein Punkt Sorgen bereitet.

nzz.title: Europas neuer Protektionismus bedroht Schweizer Autozulieferer – ist China der lachende Dritte?
nzz.description: Die EU will mit neuen Gesetzen ihre Schlüsselindustrien stärken. Nun warnt der Industrieverband Swissmem: Beschliesse die EU strenge Herkunftsregeln, gefährde sie den Zugang Schweizer Zulieferer zum europäischen Markt.

nzz.title: GASTKOMMENTAR - Die AfD vor dem Höhenflug – eine Analyse vor den Landtagswahlen in Sachsen-Anhalt, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern und Berlin
nzz.description: CDU und SPD sind im Sinkflug, AfD und Linke legen zu. Das erschwert die Bildung von homogenen Koalitionen.

nzz.title: Frauen, die kämpfen, irritieren – noch immer. Erstmals findet in Einsiedeln ein internationales Turnier nur für Ringerinnen statt
nzz.description: Das Ladies Wrestling Tournament Switzerland schreibt Schweizer Sportgeschichte. Und ein neues Buch räumt mit dem Mythos auf, dass Kämpfen männlich sei.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - «Ich verstehe die Sorgen um die Swiss. Aber manchmal kommen sie mir vor wie Phantomschmerzen»
nzz.description: Fünf Jahre lang präsidierte Johannes Teyssen den Stromkonzern Alpiq, nun führt er den Aufsichtsrat der Lufthansa. Schweizer Alleingänge seien eine Illusion, sagt er im Gespräch – ob in der Energieversorgung oder in der Luftfahrt.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - «Ich glaube, dass Putin zunehmend von der Realität entkoppelt ist»
nzz.description: Der Russland-Kenner Matthias Uhl hält die militärische Stärke des Putin-Regimes für überschätzt. Europa müsse sich dennoch auf die neue geopolitische Ära vorbereiten.

nzz.title: Trumps Plan für Europas Nationalisten hat nicht funktioniert
nzz.description: Die transatlantische Allianz zwischen der Maga-Bewegung und den europäischen Rechtspopulisten ist in der Krise. Das hat drei Gründe.

observador.title: O que acontece se Putin perder a guerra?
observador.description: Putin poderá estar mesmo a temer pela própria sobrevivência se não conseguir uma vitória na Ucrânia? Daniela Nunes explica o que pode acontecer ao regime russo se a guerra correr mal.

observador.title: 4h. Centenas de concentrações em Espanha por Ceuta
observador.description: Coincidem com Dia de Ceuta e surgem com apelos à solidariedade, “contra o racismo” e com críticas à gestão da crise pelo Governo espanhol. Ainda, Ministros da UE discutem novas sanções à Rússia

observador.title: 3h. Novos ataques norte-americanos no sudeste do Irão
observador.description: Locais perto das cidades de Ahvaz e Aghajari foram alvo de ataques, segundo a notícia avançada pela emissora estatal iraniana. Ainda, 2.ª edição do cheque-livro emitiu mais de 52 mil vouchers

observador.title: 2h. Tensões no Médio Oriente alastram a vários países
observador.description: A Guarda Revolucionária Islâmica do Irão está a atacar bases militares dos EUA no Médio Oriente. Ainda, presidente da Comissão Parlamentar que vai ouvir o MAI diz que Ventura pode estar presente

observador.title: 1h. CENTCOM anuncia fim dos ataques contra o Irão por hoje
observador.description: O Comando Central dos Estados Unidos defende sucesso e afirma que militares permanecem "preparados para continuar a executar operações”. Ainda, líder do Chega inclinado para moção de censura.

observador.title: Alemanha decide fechar o consulado-geral da Rússia
observador.description: Devido à tentativa de ataque híbrido com drones no aeroporto de Leipzig. O governo alemão determinou o encerramento formal do Consulado-Geral Russo na cidade de Bona a partir do dia 18 de setembro

observador.title: Zelensky anuncia espaço aéreo russo como fechado
observador.description: Destaque no jornal The Kyiv Independent. Zelensky alertou companhias aéreas, seguradoras e governos estrangeiros de que os céus da Rússia estão perigosos devido à atividade de drones ucranianos

observador.title: George Santos expulso da Kalshi por apostas na plataforma
observador.description: O antigo congressista afirmou que iria ao discurso do Estado da Nação, o que fez disparar as odds sobre a sua presença, mas não apareceu. Santos já tinha apostado que não iria marcar presença.

observador.title: Alguém recorde a Luís Neves que é apenas o MAI
observador.description: Luís Neves recusou demitir-se. Seja então coerente, concentre-se nas suas funções de MAI e esqueça o que não faz parte das suas competências, como o combate ao populismo.

observador.title: 25 depois do 11 de Setembro
observador.description: Fomos socializados a acreditar num referente moral fixo. Os que hoje têm vinte anos estão a ser socializados num mundo em que a América já não é o referente moral

observador.title: A nega da Islândia à União Europeia
observador.description: Seria bom que a UE aproveitasse esta rejeição para um exercício de auto-análise sobre os seus próprios problemas internos.

observador.title: Putin pretende terminar guerra, mas negociar com os EUA
observador.description: O Presidente russo garante que não quer "congelar" o conflito, mas manifesta preferência em negociar com os Estados Unidos e rejeita conversações com a Ucrânia, que apelida de "terroristas".

observador.title: Os gangues do Rolex, do Bloco e da Festa do Avante
observador.description: Para os Neves, o país é seguríssimo: relógios tirados dos pulsos, AIMIs tirados das carteiras e terroristas a tirarem-nos do sério. Por este andar, depressa o Gangue do Rolex vira o Gangue do Timex.

observador.title: 00h. Rússia tem ajudado Irão a desenvolver mísseis avançados
observador.description: É uma das transferências mais significativas de tecnologia militar estratégica de Moscovo para Teerão, segundo o jornal Financial Times. Ainda, Ventura assume que esta mais perto de avançar com moção.

observador.title: Amo Portugal, e é por isso que entro pelo Porto
observador.description: Envergonha-me um pouco, a mim que escolhi Portugal como segunda pátria do coração, ter de lhe entrar pelas traseiras.

observador.title: Plano Nacional de Restauro da Natureza
observador.description: Ao entregar o PNRN dentro do prazo, Portugal enviou uma mensagem clara: a recuperação da natureza é uma prioridade estratégica, não um acessório

observador.title: O terrorismo como ferramenta do PCP
observador.description: Para o PCP, a FPLP é apenas mais um “movimento de libertação”. Mas a História, escrita em sangue e gravada em registos oficiais, desmente a narrativa comunista.

observador.title: O Estado é deles, o povo é que paga
observador.description: Não é acusando os adversários de fascismo, nem denunciando apenas os escândalos alheios enquanto se protegem os próprios, que se trava o crescimento dos extremos

spiegel.title: Bahnprojekte: Verbändebündnis warnt vor Scheitern von mehr als 90 Vorhaben
spiegel.description: Fehlende Milliarden, verschleppte Reformen: Konzerne, Gewerkschafter und Verbände warnen, dass noch immer zu wenig Geld ins deutsche Schienennetz fließe. Das könne »erhebliche Auswirkungen auf Lieferketten« haben.

spiegel.title: Atomwächter der Uno haben 73 Tonnen Uran aus Assad-Ära in Syrien sichergestellt
spiegel.description: Der Assad-Clan träumte von einem eigenen Atomreaktor. Den Bau hat Israel vor einigen Jahren in einer Geheimmission zerstört. Nun hat die IAEA lange geheimgehaltene Uran-Bestände in Syrien sichergestellt.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: Apple folgt Trumps Umbenennung von Lake Ontario
spiegel.description: Im Handelsstreit mit Kanada hat Donald Trump den Grenzsee Lake Ontario in »Lake America« umbenannt. Nachdem Google bereits die neue Bezeichnung übernommen hatte, zieht nun auch der Techriese aus Cupertino nach.

spiegel.title: Samsung: Weltkonzern verklagt Stadt Datteln wegen Tablet-Vergabe
spiegel.description: Die Stadt Datteln wollte rund 670 Apple-Tablets bestellen. Konkurrent Samsung sah sich übergangen und zog vor Gericht. Nun wird ein Urteil erwartet, das wegweisend sein könnte.

spiegel.title: Iran kritisiert US-Sanktionen: »Verhalten aus der Steinzeit«
spiegel.description: Studenten auf der ganzen Welt kennen ihn, junge Iranerinnen und Iraner können ihn aufgrund der aktuellen Sanktionen der USA nun nicht machen: der TOEFL-Sprachtest. Das Regime in Teheran kritisiert das massiv.

spiegel.title: Chinas Cosco-Schiffe spionieren offenbar mit Hightech-Gerät Militärfunk aus
spiegel.description: Donald Trump will Xi Jinping Ende September empfangen. Kurz vor dem Spitzentreffen machen die USA nun der chinesischen Reederei Cosco schwere Vorwürfe. Das Unternehmen ist auch in Hamburg tätig.

spiegel.title: Studie der Universität Tübingen: Was macht Vogelgesang so schön?
spiegel.description: Forschende haben Probanden 123 Vogelgesänge vorgespielt und ermittelt, welche als besonders angenehm bewertet werden. Dabei fanden sie Hinweise darauf, warum die Amsel den Test gewann – und die Schleiereule verlor.

spiegel.title: Enes Kanter Freedom: Will er sich inszenieren, oder den Frauensport retten?
spiegel.description: Im US-Basketball tobt eine Debatte über die Teilnahme von trans Athletinnen. Mittendrin: Enes Kanter Freedom, Basketballer und Aktivist. Will er sich inszenieren oder den Frauensport retten? Dem SPIEGEL gibt er Antworten.

spiegel.title: »One Night Only«: Der Countdown läuft, dann startet der staatliche Sex-Tag
spiegel.description: Die romantische Komödie »One Night Only« erzählt eine sehr klassische Liebesgeschichte, aber vor einem dystopischen Hintergrund. Das könnte interessant sein – aber misslingt leider total.

spiegel.title: Anna Wintour und ihre Unterstützung für John Galliano: Hinter ihrer Sonnenbrille sah sie die Empörung nicht kommen
spiegel.description: Anna Wintour ist eine wichtige Unterstützerin des umstrittenen Designers John Galliano. Das könnte sie nun ihre Machtstellung in der Modewelt kosten.

spiegel.title: Nach 21 Jahren sind Wir sind Helden mit »Von hier an blind« wieder in den Charts. Welche Sehnsucht bedient der Song?
Ausbildung: Azubis nennen psychische Belastung als Hauptgrund für Abbruch
spiegel.description: Eine Ausbildung kann junge Menschen so sehr belasten, dass sie sich für ein frühzeitiges Ende entscheiden. Viele Unternehmen bieten deshalb Kurse zu Stressmanagement oder mentaler Gesundheit an – doch das wissen viele gar nicht.

spiegel.title: Kita-Krise: Warum es trotz sinkender Kinderzahlen weiter Probleme gibt

phys-org.title: Scientists discover the key ingredients that make birdsong pretty
phys-org.description: What makes birdsong beautiful? Answering this question could help us understand how soundscapes make the natural world relaxing for humans, opening the door to improving parks, upgrading the design of stressful places like waiting rooms and promoting conservation through birds with especially lovely songs.

phys-org.title: Community-led systems may curb illegal dumping in Indonesia's rural tourism areas
phys-org.description: Local action may offer a model for waste management in rural tourism, according to research published in the International Journal of Tourism Anthropology. The study of waste problems in Kampung Nipah, a coastal tourism hamlet in North Sumatra, Indonesia, argues that rural communities with limited public services may need locally governed waste systems rather than relying solely on municipal services.

phys-org.title: Children's picture books reflect changing attitudes to languages and can support revitalization
phys-org.description: We know from a wealth of research that children's picture books support language learning.

phys-org.title: Agentic AI accelerates search for crops that can harvest critical minerals
phys-org.description: For too long, the United States has relied on foreign sources for most of the raw materials powering its technological future: the essential minerals in every smartphone, battery pack and semiconductor. What if one answer to the supply crisis isn't buried in a mine shaft but growing quietly in a field? Scientists are betting on a resource-efficient, highly effective strategy: using engineered plants and symbiotic microbes to absorb critical minerals directly from the Earth in a process call

phys-org.title: Many space missions are searching for life beyond Earth, but are we prepared for the fallout if they succeed?
phys-org.description: Microbes from space have fueled the plots of science fiction mainstays like "Project Hail Mary" and "The Andromeda Strain." But with more space missions launching each year, finding extraterrestrial life in a microbial form is becoming more plausible. What will the response be back here on Earth if—or when—scientists discover extraterrestrial microbes? Will the international policy and security communities be prepared for the fallout?

phys-org.title: Border toy screening finds 12% exceed toxic-metal limits
phys-org.description: Nearly four out of five children's toys purchased in the El Paso-Ciudad Juárez region contain at least one toxic element, according to a new study led by researchers at The University of Texas at El Paso. The findings, just published in the journal Environmental Pollution, represent the first binational screening of hazardous metals in toys sold on both sides of the U.S.-Mexico border.

phys-org.title: Magnetic beads streamline large-scale analysis of disease-linked glycopeptides
phys-org.description: A research team has developed a reliable, economical laboratory method that uses tiny magnetic beads to study proteins with sugar molecules attached to them in blood and tissue samples. A better understanding of their pathological changes could help researchers diagnose and treat diseases, including cancer.

phys-org.title: New high-temperature, high-pressure isotope ratio analysis method developed for halogenated compounds
phys-org.description: Halogenated organic compounds (HOCs) are widely used in industrial and consumer products, but some are highly persistent and difficult to analyze and manage. In a new study, researchers developed an innovative approach for carbon isotope ratio analysis of these compounds, which has previously been difficult. This approach will help track the sources and environmental pathways of such pollutants, contributing to the development of effective management strategies.

phys-org.title: Single amino acid swap expands nanoparticle vaccine approach to influenza viruses
phys-org.description: Influenza viruses constantly shapeshift to evade recognition by the immune system. This shapeshifting occurs in critical proteins like hemagglutinin (HA), which controls how the virus attaches to human cells before entering them. It provides high-resolution snapshots of biological processes. However, it does not track the same cell continuously over time. To address this limitation, trajectory inference approaches have been developed

phys-org.title: Firelight may have sparked human storytelling by extending social hours
phys-org.description: New research from the University of St Andrews has developed a novel hypothesis of how firelight was critical to the evolution of sophisticated storytelling.

phys-org.title: Muddying the waters makes stickleback fish more coordinated, study finds
phys-org.description: Stickleback fish can change their social behavior to help them find food in cloudy water, according to a new University of Bristol study published in Proceedings of the Royal Society B.

phys-org.title: Survey reveals marine biodiversity hotspot needs protection
phys-org.description: An environmental DNA study by a multi-institutional research collaboration has revealed distinct regions of extraordinary marine biodiversity that can help inform management of a proposed marine park in Western Australia's Exmouth Gulf.

phys-org.title: LEDs let archaeologists see the past in a new light
phys-org.description: An archaeological excavation is a little like eating a layered cake: Once you have removed a layer, you cannot put it back. The problem becomes even trickier if two layers look almost exactly the same. Researchers from Aarhus University and Moesgaard Museum in Denmark have now developed a relatively inexpensive multispectral imaging system that gives archaeologists more ways of looking at the soil before they dig into it.

phys-org.title: To promote climate action, emotion may matter more than information
phys-org.description: Every year, public authorities and nongovernmental organizations spend millions on communication campaigns designed to encourage people to take action on climate change. But which strategies work best? Should campaigns rely on fear or positive messages, prioritize facts or appeal to emotions, and focus on words or visuals?

phys-org.title: Giant impact could have formed an intact moon within five hours, simulations suggest
phys-org.description: New Southwest Research Institute (SwRI) modeling, conducted in collaboration with scientists at the University of Arizona, shows fundamental differences in how the moon may have formed from the giant impact that created the Earth–moon system. The new results used state-of-the-art computational techniques that factor in the material strength of the two colliding planets. These impact simulations could change how researchers understand moon formation and may help constrain the timing of the event.

phys-org.title: Elementary school teachers report increased student hunger and anxiety after universal free school meals ended
phys-org.description: A recent study published in the Journal of Nutrition Education and Behavior explored elementary school teachers' experiences before and after the end of the federal universal free school meals (UFSM) policy. Researchers found that teachers perceived the policy had helped reduce student hunger and family stress, while its expiration was associated with increased hunger, anxiety about meal costs and decreased participation in school meal programs.

phys-org.title: Salt of the Earth: How Egypt's coastal sabkhas tell a story of climate and change
phys-org.description: Have you ever walked across a salt flat so expansive it feels like another planet? That's what it's like standing in Egypt's coastal sabkhas—those otherworldly landscapes where the ground crunches beneath your feet and the air shimmers with heat. These aren't just barren wastelands; they're living laboratories that record the pulse of our changing climate.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

proj-syn.title: Hard Lessons for Europe From the Ceuta Crisis
proj-syn.description: European Union leaders should have received several messages during the recent surge of migrants into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta. In particular, cohesion without trust is fragile; dependence without limits leads to vulnerability; and selective enforcement of international law risks eroding a pillar of Europe’s strategic identity.

proj-syn.title: The World’s Silent Majority for International Cooperation
proj-syn.description: The hollowing out of global institutions has resulted in a rapid loss of credibility for the international rule of law. But a majority of people worldwide still recognize the value of multilateralism, which countries can preserve in the absence of superpower consent by finding better ways to cooperate.

proj-syn.title: Building Canada’s Post-American Economy
proj-syn.description: Canada’s dependence on the US market has become a strategic liability, leaving it vulnerable to President Donald Trump’s bullying. Reducing that dependence will require building industries that can compete globally while removing the structural barriers that prevent innovative Canadian firms from scaling.

proj-syn.title: Trump and Xi Should Align on AI
proj-syn.description: When potential outcomes are systemic and irreversible, preparation must precede certainty. This is the logic behind insurance, as well as every pandemic plan and arms-control treaty ever created, and it must be the principle that guides our approach to AI—beginning at the upcoming US-China summit.

proj-syn.title: The Quiet Revolution in Services
proj-syn.description: While economists debate whether industrialization can still play its traditional growth-promoting role in the current global and technological context, services have unexpectedly become an engine for economic development around the world. For developing and developed economies alike, the timing could not be better.

proj-syn.title: AI Addicts Won’t Make Better Workers
proj-syn.description: Economists widely agree that AI will boost labor productivity. But this view does not account for the possibility that hyperscalers will go all out to get people hooked on LLMs, because the narrower applications for which these tools are actually useful do not justify the massive investments made so far.

proj-syn.title: Latin America’s Crime Tax
proj-syn.description: Even excluding lives lost, communities displaced, and families ravaged, the economic costs of organized crime in the region produce a bleak picture, shaving 0.5–2 percentage points off annual GDP growth in the most affected countries. That, too, represents a hefty human toll.

proj-syn.title: Are The Walls Closing in on Bessent?
proj-syn.description: Far from suggesting financial Armageddon, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s futile efforts to keep a lid on Treasury yields suggest that, once again, the dollar is America’s currency, but everyone else’s problem. But while investors have few alternatives, the bond-salesman-in-chief cannot be complacent.

proj-syn.title: AI Is Reviving Chinese Marxist Economics
proj-syn.description: As recently as two years ago, most Chinese economists paid only lip service to Marxism and assigned Western textbooks to their students. The advent of AI has changed that, because the technology—open source and available to the smallest manufacturer for a pittance—promises to avoid the “rent trap” common to capitalist economies.

proj-syn.title: Gen Z Is Transforming South Asia
proj-syn.description: Facing diminished economic prospects, many young people see not flawed institutions in need of gradual reform, but predatory systems robbing them of their future. Across South Asia, this sense has animated powerful protest movements, some of which could shape their countries' political trajectories for decades to come.

proj-syn.title: How Britain Can Help Build a Fairer Global Economy
proj-syn.description: With the United Kingdom poised to preside over both the G20 and the G7, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has a unique opportunity to usher in a new internationalism grounded not in military posturing, but in the pursuit of a fairer global economy. But he must abandon his predecessor’s defensive approach.

proj-syn.title: Technocracy Can’t Fix Europe
proj-syn.description: A new private initiative bringing together the crème de la crème of European business, financial, economic, and tech elites could well prove useful in kick-starting European growth and innovation. But first, it must recognize that the problem it hopes to solve is fundamentally political.

proj-syn.title: The Fed and the Treasury Are in Denial
proj-syn.description: For most of the postwar era, the United States has enjoyed a privileged position as an issuer of both sovereign debt and US dollars that always found takers. But the US may no longer be able to rely on stable demand for its debt or its currency, forcing policymakers to face the truth about how financial markets are made.

proj-syn.title: To End Global Hunger, Invest in Rural Communities
proj-syn.description: Even as hunger declines around the world, food insecurity remains prevalent in rural communities. Restoring soil health, expanding access to new technologies, strengthening land rights, and upgrading public infrastructure are essential to boost agricultural productivity and protect rural livelihoods.

proj-syn.title: The Sanctions Illusion
proj-syn.description: Those who defend sweeping financial sanctions against countries like Russia and Iran often claim that popular suffering is a defensible means of pressuring the target government. But while such measures certainly inflict widespread suffering on civilian populations, this rarely translates into political change.

proj-syn.title: Is Monetarism Making a Comeback?
proj-syn.description: After decades on the margins of mainstream economic thinking, monetarism is beginning to re-enter the debate, most notably at the Federal Reserve. To regain credibility, however, monetarists must learn from past mistakes and adapt to the monetary and financial realities of the 21st century.

proj-syn.title: China’s Super-Dam Is Becoming an Upstream Water Bomb
proj-syn.description: The latest evidence suggests that the Chinese scientific establishment understands the dangers of a planned Himalayan dam—the world's largest—more clearly than its political leadership is willing to acknowledge. With the livelihoods of two billion people at stake, the international community needs to weigh in.

proj-syn.title: Europe and the War in Ukraine
proj-syn.description: If Europe remains a mere collection of small states and middle powers, the current period of profound geopolitical and historical change will also mark the end of its role on the world stage. With no end in sight for Russia's war in Ukraine, Europeans must come to grips with reality.
